points.quote: The use of AI detection software for the detection or investigation of alleged academic misconduct is not sanctioned by the University
points.gist: The Academic Integrity policy states AI detection software is not sanctioned for detecting or investigating alleged misconduct.

points.quote: students may be required to orally defend their work and understanding of the topic(s) being assessed in the case of suspected unauthorised use of GenAI.
points.gist: Students may be required to orally defend their work where unauthorised GenAI use is suspected.

points.quote: it is very important to set clear expectations on the use of GenAI in relation to your particular module/assessments. This can take the form of a GenAI Statement that you include in your course syllabus, in Canvas, and/or in assignment briefs.
points.gist: Staff should set clear module expectations, for example a GenAI Statement in the syllabus, Canvas or assignment briefs.

points.quote: it is important that expectations are made clear in each module and that students are aware of these.
points.anchor: Considerations for Using GenAI in Education
points.gist: Rules may vary from module to module, so expectations must be made clear in each module and students made aware.

points.quote: Educators should not run student work through any AI detector tools that are external to their institution as most of these tools train on content that is submitted to them
points.gist: Educators should not run student work through AI detectors external to the institution, as most train on submitted content.

points.quote: Acknowledgement that the author has reviewed and evaluated all AI-generated content and confirmed that it accurately reflects their understanding and intended meaning, along with acceptance of responsibility for the content and its accuracy.
points.gist: A declaration might include acknowledgement that the author reviewed all AI content and accepts responsibility for it and its accuracy.

points.quote: What GenAI tool(s) and version were used
points.gist: A declaration might state which GenAI tool(s) and version were used.

points.quote: Article 50 of the EU AI Act came into force in August 2026.
points.anchor: Article 50 of the EU AI Act and Transparency Obligations
points.gist: Article 50 of the EU AI Act came into force in August 2026.

points.quote: The Academic Integrity Fundamentals course, available to all UCC students in the Canvas Success Zone contains a module on the responsible use of GenAI
points.anchor: Considerations for Using GenAI in Education
points.gist: The Academic Integrity Fundamentals course in the Canvas Success Zone has a module on responsible GenAI use.

points.quote: the same standards or expectations around the responsible use of GenAI apply equally to staff and to students, ensuring transparency and fairness.
points.gist: The same standards for responsible GenAI use apply equally to staff and students.

points.quote: GenAI is known to “hallucinate” and is not credible as a source.
points.gist: GenAI is known to hallucinate and is not credible as a source.

points.quote: University staff can model this for students by acknowledging their own use of GenAI and explaining how and why they used it.
points.anchor: Considerations for Using GenAI in Education
points.gist: Staff can model transparency by acknowledging their own GenAI use and explaining how and why they used it.
